evals.prompt: Design an immersive WebXR experience for a chemistry lab simulation where students can interact with virtual molecules, mix chemicals, and observe reactions. Must work on Quest 3 and have a browser fallback.
evals.expected_output: Proposes WebXR API usage with Three.js or A-Frame, defines hand tracking interactions, designs progressive enhancement with 2D fallback, addresses performance budgets.
assertions: Designs the XR experience using WebXR APIs with a specific framework recommendation
Includes hand tracking or controller-based interaction for molecule manipulation
Provides a functional non-XR browser fallback with progressive enhancement

evals.prompt: Our WebAssembly physics simulation module is 8MB and takes 4 seconds to initialize. Students abandon the page before it loads. Optimize the WASM module.
evals.expected_output: Proposes streaming compilation, lazy loading, module splitting, compression, and a loading UX strategy to keep students engaged during init.
assertions: Recommends WASM streaming compilation to reduce perceived load time
Proposes module splitting or lazy loading to load only required physics modules
Suggests a loading UX strategy (progress bar, mini-game) to reduce abandonment

evals.prompt: Design multimodal interaction patterns for an XR anatomy learning experience. Students should be able to use voice commands, hand gestures, and gaze to explore a 3D human body model.
evals.expected_output: Defines specific voice commands for navigation, gesture vocabulary for manipulation, gaze-based selection, and how the three modalities complement each other.
assertions: Defines a voice command vocabulary for navigation and labeling
Designs hand gesture interactions for rotating, zooming, and selecting body parts
Includes gaze-based selection as a complementary input method

evals.prompt: We need to support XR experiences across Meta Quest 3, Apple Vision Pro, and standard desktop browsers. What is the device compatibility strategy and performance budget for each?
evals.expected_output: Creates a compatibility matrix, defines rendering budgets per device, proposes adaptive quality levels, and identifies feature gaps between platforms.
assertions: Creates a device compatibility matrix covering all three target platforms
Defines different performance budgets (polygon count, draw calls, frame rate) per device tier
Proposes adaptive quality levels that scale with device capabilities

evals.prompt: Evaluate whether to use WebAssembly or JavaScript for our real-time 3D graph visualization that renders 10,000 nodes with physics-based layout. Current JS implementation runs at 12fps.
evals.expected_output: Benchmarks WASM vs JS for this workload, quantifies expected FPS improvement, considers compilation complexity, and recommends a hybrid approach if warranted.
assertions: Compares WebAssembly and JavaScript performance for the specific 10K node rendering workload
Estimates the FPS improvement achievable with WASM
Considers the added complexity of WASM and recommends the justified approach

should_trigger: Design a WebXR experience for our virtual lab simulation
Optimize our WebAssembly module that is too slow to load
